clue.text: Well-wisher right in the grip of a demon

indicators.note: being in the grip of something means being held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a fiend is a demon

explanation.surface: A supposed well-wisher turns out to be firmly held by a demon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal or ally is someone who wishes you well.

clue.text: Careless girl about to take the lead

indicators.note: taking the lead means going in front, so this piece comes before the other

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A careless young woman is about to step out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take the lead' places RE (about) ahead of MISS (girl).
explanation.definitionFit: Being remiss means being negligent in one's duties.

parts.note: the classic British takeaway is battered cod with fried potatoes, sold from a dedicated shop

explanation.definitionFit: The chippy is the archetypal British outlet selling battered fish and fried potatoes to take away.

clue.text: Plead to cut short the starter at last

indicators.note: last says this piece comes at the end of the answer
cutting something short removes its final letter, here from the word for the starter

parts.note: an entree is a starter course at dinner

explanation.surface: A diner begs to have the first course cut short at long last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' trims ENTREE to ENTRE; 'last' puts AT after it. 'at last' looks like a phrase meaning finally.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or implore earnestly.

definitions.meaning: an idiom telling someone to stay calm and not lose their temper
read literally, keeping one's top garment on the body

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges calm, and literally it means remaining clothed in a top garment.

parts.note: usually means took extra trouble, but here literally means took a roundabout route

explanation.definitionFit: Taking a roundabout route away from the direct road is the literal sense of the phrase.

parts.note: Des is the short form of the name Desmond

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked over and made ready, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A domineering man named Desmond had readied a subject for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges DES (short for Desmond) plus TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a tyrant, so despotic behaviour is autocratic and oppressive.

indicators.note: first says the piece before it goes at the front of the answer

parts.note: fries means cooks in hot fat
Ian is a typically Scottish boy's name

explanation.surface: A Scottish lad cooks a cow before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts FRIES (cooks) before IAN, reversing the clue's order. A FRIESIAN is a black-and-white dairy breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Friesian is a breed of black-and-white dairy cattle.

clue.text: Still behind the Spanish footballers perhaps

indicators.note: behind means this piece follows the one named after it

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
still as in yet more so, matching even in 'even better'

explanation.surface: Spanish footballers are still trailing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts EVEN after EL. 'Still' means 'even' as in 'even/still better'.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side fields a team of that many players.

indicators.note: centrally points to the middle letters of the words not held

explanation.surface: An article was not kept in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The definite article in English grammar.

clue.text: Make out meaning of price he'd fabricated

indicators.note: fabricated means made up or constructed, so these letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to understand the cost he had invented.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a message is to work out what it says.

definitions.meaning: in theatre, to feed a forgetful actor the next line

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre helper cues an actor's forgotten line, and an immediate reply is on time.

clue.text: You can bet it is most likely to win

definitions.text: You can bet it is most likely to win

parts.words: You can bet it is most likely to win
parts.note: a pun on 'you can bet': the horse priced shortest by bookmakers is the one expected to win

explanation.definitionFit: In betting, the runner priced below evens is expected to come home first.

clue.text: Little point in being a lady?

definitions.meaning: a woman's name, short for Dorothy

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny mark is a speck, and Dot is a pet form of Dorothy.

parts.note: the three letters are the word cut written backwards; TUC is also Britain's Trades Union Congress

explanation.surface: The trade union body faces a spending decrease.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC (Trades Union Congress) is Britain's federation of trade unions, which would oppose spending reductions.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction in spending is a common term in budget politics.

indicators.note: overturned means knocked over and upset, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Anne calls it nonsense that our decision was overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of reason, irrationality, is absurdity.

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means this piece sits above the next

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for loading ships

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about a scoundrel aboard a British vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places B over LIGHTER in this down clue. 'Blighter' is a mild British insult for a rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighter is British slang for an annoying or contemptible person.

clue.text: Disheartened pair with proclamation to foretell

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the outer letters of the word pair remain

parts.note: an edict is an official proclamation

explanation.surface: A dejected couple issue an announcement to prophesy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' strips AI from PAIR to leave PR, then EDICT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To prophesy is to say beforehand what will happen.

parts.note: mounted as in up on a horse or stand

explanation.surface: Someone climbed up for a minor fee.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrically charged atom or molecule carries a tiny charge.

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of ancient times
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A pious ascetic lived to around a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ESSENE round C. The Essenes were an ancient Jewish sect.
explanation.definitionFit: One's essence is one's fundamental nature or existence.

clue.text: Is it plain sailing in it?

definitions.text: Is it plain sailing in it?

parts.words: Is it plain sailing in it?
parts.note: plain sailing means easy going, but here a plain is grassland and sailing suggests a ship

explanation.definitionFit: A covered wagon used by American pioneers crossing the grasslands, named after a sailing ship.

clue.text: Set so as to face right on a map of Asia

definitions.text: Set so as to face right on a map
definitions.meaning: to align toward the east, which is on the right of a map
the East, the countries of Asia

explanation.definitionFit: To align something is to position it, originally eastward, and the East names Asia.

indicators.note: letting something go means losing it, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: letting a property is leasing it
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A landlord is unwinding after giving up fifty properties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting 50 go' drops L from LEASING. Letting is renting out.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosening tension or slackening off is becoming less tight.

clue.text: It's an anticlimax for bachelor meeting new host

indicators.note: meeting means coming together, so the pieces are joined side by side

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, giving the letter A

indicators.note: new means freshly made, so the letters are remade in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A single man is disappointed to meet a new host.
explanation.walkthrough: The A comes from 'an'; 'new' rearranges HOST to THOS, and 'meeting' joins B to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is a ludicrous drop from the elevated to the trivial.

indicators.note: has means the first piece is followed by the second

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or irregular, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A leading aristocrat wears oddball neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest means soonest of all, the very first.

parts.note: a layer here is not a stratum but one that lays eggs, sitting in its nest

explanation.definitionFit: A female chicken lays eggs.

parts.note: ego is the Latin word for I, the self

explanation.surface: Someone decides to depart for their own sake.
explanation.definitionFit: To do without something is to give it up.

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
owning, as in owning up, means admitting

explanation.surface: A form of pupils confesses to fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' looks like a container signal but means OWNING, as in 'owning up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a jester is behaving comically.
